I'd like to verify by actually running a refund message through tryTriage, but that needs a Gemini API key, so let me check if one's set in the environment first.

The chat flow matches what the user described: triage is handling the conversation directly and delegating to orderAgent for order questions, which is consistent with refunds breaking once refundAgent dropped off the list. Time to make the fix.

The middleware injects one delegation tool per name in `agents`, so with only `orderAgent` listed, the triage model has no `refundAgent` tool to call. Order questions still work through `orderAgent`, which matches the report. I'll check whether a Gemini key is available for a live before/after run.

The refund agent correctly raises an approveRefund interrupt with the amount and reason for the direct desk path. In the triage path, though, the sub-agent's interrupt gets surfaced back to the orchestrator as a regular tool response rather than a true interrupt, which is why the triage model just asked for more info instead of pausing for approval.

The real bug here is the missing delegation to the refund agent — that's the root cause I need to fix in the app's source. The lack of interrupt propagation through sub-agents is a known middleware limitation marked as a future feature, so fixing that would be scope creep beyond the actual reported bug.

I also noticed `.genkit/` got created during my test runs; since it didn't exist before and is just a session artifact I generated, I'll clean it up before finishing.

Also /tmp/repro is outside the project directory, so I should remove that too. For the answer, I'll reference the exact broken line from src/agents.ts verbatim so the match is unambiguous, and place the final answer.json at the project root.

The core cause is that the triage agent's `agents()` middleware only lists orderAgent, so it never gets a delegation tool for refundAgent and ends up refusing refund requests itself. My evidence: before the fix, asking the triage agent for a refund returned a canned refusal with no delegation call; after adding refundAgent to the list, it properly delegates and calls approveRefund, while shipping-status questions still resolve correctly — confirming the middleware builds one delegate_to tool per listed agent. Let me double-check this evidence is accurate before finalizing.

Since I only observed the reply text and not an explicit tool-call list, I should phrase it as "returned a refusal instead of delegating" rather than asserting no tool call was made. After the fix, the triage reply explicitly says it delegated to the refund agent, which supports the conclusion well enough.

Now I'll write this up to the answer file, then clean up the .genkit directory and /tmp/repro, and run a quick `npx tsc --noEmit` to confirm everything still compiles.

The refund agent works when called directly: it calls `approveRefund` for A-1001 at 149.99. The leftover gap is that the middleware reports a sub-agent's interrupt back to triage as a tool response, so the chat asks the customer for more details instead of showing an approval prompt. That's a middleware limitation rather than this bug, so I'll flag it rather than redesign routing. Next I'll type-check, write `answer.json`, and clean up the `.genkit/` session store and scratch files my test runs created.

The root cause is in `src/agents.ts`: the triage agent's `agents()` middleware only lists `orderAgent`, so the model never gets a tool to delegate to `refundAgent`. It answers refund requests itself with a refusal, while order-status questions still reach `orderAgent`.

I changed the list to `['orderAgent', 'refundAgent']` (line 55). Before the fix, the refund message got "I cannot process refund requests." After it, the message is delegated to the refund agent, which calls `approveRefund` for A-1001 (149.99). The order question still returns the correct status. `tsc --noEmit` passes, and `package.json` is unchanged.

One gap remains. The middleware reports a sub-agent's approval interrupt back to triage as a tool response, so the chat currently asks the customer for more details instead of showing an approval prompt. Fixing that means changing how the approval step surfaces, which I didn't attempt. Say if you want that.

`answer.json` is written at the project root. I deleted the `.genkit/` session store that my test runs created.
